description: Five reports provided information to Council.
Council requested a report on shelter separation distances from childcare.
This report will include practices from other Western Canadian cities.

chips.text: Councillor Dubois expressed sadness for vulnerable children in daycares near shelters.
90 children aged 18 months to five years at YWCA childcare facility.
Delegates reported drug activity and safety issues near proposed drop-in center.
Administration committed to extending safety patrols to daycare entrances if directed.

speakers.name: Sara Wheelwright
speakers.summary: Sara Wheelwright addressed Committee expressing concerns about locating the proposed drop‑in centre near a childcare facility, citing observed safety issues in the area, and urged Council to formalize separation distance requirements and...
said: Proximity matters; 250m school buffer should extend to daycares.
Proposed drop-in center 30 steps from YWCA daycare (90 children).
Witnessed drug activity/paraphernalia near daycare playground; relocate drop-in.

speakers.name: Shawna Nelson
speakers.summary: Shawna Nelson addressed Committee emphasizing the need to formalize and expand separation distance requirements, citing impacts observed near existing sites.
said: Formalize 250m separation bylaw for shelters, drop-ins, daycares, schools.
Avenue C shows impacts: drug use, disorder; 130 Idylwyld will be similar.
Unsafe to place high-impact facilities near daycares; fund safety plans.

chips.text: Councillor Dubois expressed frustration over city funding provincial responsibilities.
Residents and businesses near Avenue C and public washroom.
When the 20-year outdated SHA contract for medical calls will be sorted out.
Delegate praised coordinated safety plan at Pacific Avenue shelter as effective.
Provides meaningful support to vulnerable individuals using drop-in centers.

speakers.name: Timothy Cain
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Community Safety Update - Service Levels for Ave C
said: Past shelter at 145 2nd Ave North increased crime, disorder.
Coordinated safety plan at Pacific Avenue shelter proved highly effective.
Urges Council to adopt maximum funding option for these initiatives.
